headline: New graph, autoencoder and language-model methods impose structure on omics data
label: Single Cell Pattern Inference
summary: Explicit structural models now target single-cell and scATAC-seq data to recover organization flat representations may miss.
synthesis: The dominant thread is imposing explicit structure on high-dimensional omics data to recover organization that flat representations may not capture. Three of the four items operate on single-cell data: scConcept couples neural topic modeling with LLMs to map gene-level topics onto individual cells as labeled biological concepts; a k-MST graph algorithm and an autoencoder-based Gaussian mixture alternative address unsupervised scRNA-seq cell clustering with benchmarks; and scLLMDA annotates scATAC-seq cell types by combining DNA language model peak embeddings with graph neural network domain adaptation. The AMD study generalizes MEGENA co-expression clustering on RNA-Seq data with new similarity measures and a hub-gene stability test. What is new is the pairing of language-model representations with graph-based structure. No item addresses spatial organization.
